basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/WhoisXML%20API/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The WhoisXML API solution for Microsoft Sentinel ingests three WhoisXML API feeds (Newly Registered Domains 2.0, Threat Intelligence and Bulk Registration Risk) and matches them against your DNS, web proxy, endpoint and email logs. **Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:** This solution takes a dependency on the following technologies, and some of these dependencies either may be in [Preview](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/) state or might result in additional ingestion or operational costs: a. [Codeless Connector Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/create-codeless-connector) b. [Data Collection Rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/essentials/data-collection-rule-overview) **Prerequisites:** a WhoisXML API key with a subscription to the feeds you enable. Rules use the ASIM DNS and Web Session parsers and Microsoft Defender XDR tables where present. **Data Connectors:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 6, **Hunting Queries:** 3, **Watchlists:** 3 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This Solution installs the data connector for WhoisXML API Domain Feeds (via Codeless Connector Framework). You can get WhoisXML API Domain Feeds (via Codeless Connector Framework) data in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace. After installing the solution, configure and enable this data connector by following guidance in Manage solution view.

link.label: Learn more about connecting data sources

options.text: This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.

elements.name: analytic1
elements.label: WhoisXML API - Newly registered domain resolved by internal host

options.text: Identifies hosts that resolved a domain WhoisXML API lists as newly registered in the last 14 days. New domains are common in phishing, malware delivery and command and control.

elements.name: analytic2
elements.label: WhoisXML API - Newly registered domain linked in delivered email

options.text: Identifies inbound email delivered to a mailbox that links to a domain WhoisXML API lists as newly registered in the last 14 days. Links to very young domains are a strong phishing signal.

elements.name: analytic3
elements.label: WhoisXML API - User clicked link to newly registered domain

options.text: Identifies users who clicked a link in email, Teams or Office apps to a domain WhoisXML API lists as newly registered in the last 14 days, where the click was allowed or the user clicked through a warning.

elements.name: analytic4
elements.label: WhoisXML API - Threat intelligence domain resolved by internal host

options.text: Identifies hosts that resolved a domain listed in the WhoisXML API Threat Intelligence feed. Severity depends on the threat type, how recently WhoisXML API observed the domain, and whether it sits under a widely used domain other than a hosting platform.

elements.name: analytic5
elements.label: WhoisXML API - Connection to threat intelligence domain from endpoint or proxy

options.text: Identifies endpoint connections and web proxy requests to a domain listed in the WhoisXML API Threat Intelligence feed, using Defender for Endpoint, ASIM web session and CEF proxy logs.

elements.name: analytic6
elements.label: WhoisXML API - Lookalike of your brand resolved by internal host

options.text: Identifies hosts that resolved a WhoisXML API Bulk Registration Risk (typosquatting) domain that contains one of your brand keywords. Add your keywords to the WhoisXMLBrandKeywordsCustom watchlist.
This solution installs the following hunting queries. After installing the solution, run these hunting queries to hunt for threats in Manage solution view.

elements.name: huntingquery1
elements.label: WhoisXML API - DNS lookups that preceded a domain's listing as newly registered

options.text: This query searches for DNS lookups in the last 3 days of domains whose WhoisXML API newly registered domain rows first reached this workspace in the last day, so lookups made before the domain was listed are not missed. This hunting query depends on WhoisXMLAPIFeeds DNS data connector (WhoisXMLNRD_CL DnsEvents Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery2
elements.label: WhoisXML API - Lookalikes of your brand in the typosquatting feed

options.text: This query searches for domains in the last 14 days of the WhoisXML API Bulk Registration Risk (typosquatting) feed that contain a keyword from your brand keyword watchlists, whether or not anyone resolved them. This hunting query depends on WhoisXMLAPIFeeds data connector (WhoisXMLTyposquatting_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery3
elements.label: WhoisXML API - Bulk registration groups resolved from your estate

options.text: This query searches for WhoisXML API Bulk Registration Risk groups of the last 14 days with two or more member domains resolved in your DNS logs, a sign of a campaign rather than a single lookalike. This hunting query depends on WhoisXMLAPIFeeds DNS data connector (WhoisXMLTyposquatting_CL DnsEvents Parser or Table)

Microsoft Sentinel watchlists enable the collection of data from external data sources for correlation with the events in your Microsoft Sentinel environment. Once created, you can use watchlists in your search, detection rules, threat hunting, and response playbooks. Watchlists are stored in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace as name-value pairs and are cached for optimal query performance and low latency. Once deployment is successful, the installed watchlists will be available in the Watchlists blade under 'My Watchlists'.

Example brand keywords for the WhoisXML API brand-lookalike rule and hunting query. The rules ignore these placeholder rows, and this list is reset on every solution update. Put your own brand keywords (one per row, column Keyword) in a watchlist you create with the alias WhoisXMLBrandKeywordsCustom.

Example domain allowlist for the WhoisXML API rules. Rules ignore domains listed here, and this list is reset on every solution update. Put the domains you want the rules to ignore (one per row, column Domain) in a watchlist you create with the alias WhoisXMLDomainAllowlistCustom.

Hosting platforms where each subdomain is a different party's site, such as free website hosts, site builders and dynamic DNS services. A threat intelligence listing under one of these keeps its severity instead of becoming informational for sitting under a popular domain. This list is replaced on every solution update; add platforms in a watchlist you create with the alias WhoisXMLHostingPlatformsCustom.
